results.title: Payroll tax
results.description:
# Payroll tax
[About payroll tax\
\
A State and Territory tax on the wages that employers pay employees and contractors.](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/business-taxes-and-levies/payroll-tax/about-payroll-tax) [Grouping\
\
Find out how related entities and trusts may be grouped for the purposes of payroll tax.](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/business-taxes-and-levies/payroll-tax/grouping) [Contractors\
\
Find out how payroll tax applies to contractors and subcontractors.](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/business-taxes-and-levies/payroll-tax/contractors) [Registration\
\
Employers who pay taxable wages that exceed the ACT’s monthly threshold must register for payroll tax.](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/business-taxes-and-levies/payroll-tax/registration) [Lodging returns\
\
Employers who operate in the ACT and exceed the Australia-wide tax-free threshold must lodge payroll tax returns.](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/business-taxes-and-levies/payroll-tax/lodging-returns) [Calculating payroll tax\
\
Find out how we calculate your payroll tax and the tax-free threshold.](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/business-taxes-and-levies/payroll-tax/calculating-payroll-tax) [Designated medical practices with General Practitioners\
\
Find out how payroll tax applies to designated medical practices with contractor General Practitioners.](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/business-taxes-and-levies/payroll-tax/designated-medical-practices-with-general-practitioners)

From 1 July 2026, the Payroll Tax Act 2009 will be amended to introduce a higher payroll tax rate of 6.5% for employers, and members of payroll tax groups, with Australia-wide wages of $100 million or more. The amendments leave the current $2.5 million tax free threshold, deduction settings and general 5.5% rate unchanged for all other employers.
